svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.22.7.1 Slope of Smoke Chamber
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.22.7.1 Slope of Smoke Chamber
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.22 FIREPLACES

g.text: Sides set in 290 mm over a 400 mm rise:
Sides set in 290 mm over a 200 mm rise:
CHECKING THE ANGLE, EXAMPLE, ILLUSTRATION ONLY
Angle to the vertical = arctan (set-in ÷ rise)
The set-in is how far one side moves inward, the rise is the height it takes to do it.
290 mm over 400 mm: 36°. 290 mm over 200 mm: 55°.
At 45° the set-in equals the rise, so a set-in larger than the rise is too flat.

svg.text: The sides of the smoke chamber connecting a
fireplace throat with a flue are not sloped at
an angle greater than 45° to the vertical.
Drawn: cut through the throat and smoke chamber, seen from the front. Angles look different in this view, the figures given are the true angles.
